name: Dou Dizhu
description: Dou Dizhu (Fight the Landlord) is a Chinese climbing game for three players. One player becomes the landlord by winning an auction (bid 1, 2 or 3) and plays alone against the other two in partnership. Players shed cards by playing singles or valid combinations; the landlord leads and each player in turn must pass or beat the previous play. Rocket (two jokers) and bomb (four of a kind) are special combinations. The first side to empty their hand wins the hand; payment is the bid amount times multipliers for bombs and rockets.

content.text: Dou Dizhu (Fight the Landlord) is a Chinese climbing game for three players. One player becomes the landlord by winning an auction (bid 1, 2 or 3) and plays alone against the other two in partnership. Players shed cards by playing singles or valid combinations; the landlord leads and each player in turn must pass or beat the previous play. Rocket (two jokers) and bomb (four of a kind) are special combinations. The first side to empty their hand wins the hand; payment is the bid amount times multipliers for bombs and rockets.

Dou Dizhu is said to have originated in Hubei province. The name (literally 'fighting the landlord') reflects the class struggle during China's land reform of the 1950s, when peasants were encouraged to oppose landlords. The game has become very popular across China in the last twenty years and is widely played online; the name no longer carries negative connotation.
Three players; four-player variant uses a double deck.
54-card pack: standard 52 cards plus two jokers (red and black). Suits are irrelevant; rank from high to low is red joker, black joker, 2, A, K, Q, J, 10 down to 3.
Standard 52-card deck plus two jokers (red and black).

One player shuffles and gives the deck to the player to his left to cut. Cards are stacked face down in the centre. One card is turned face up and inserted near the middle to determine who starts the auction. Players then draw from the top counter-clockwise: each looks at their card without showing. Drawing continues until each player has 17 cards. The last three cards remain face down until after the auction; the winning bidder (landlord) adds them to their hand for 20 cards total.
